ground_truth.root_cause_analysis: The billing-service JVM container exceeded the 16Gi memory limit specified in its Kubernetes resource quota, triggering the Linux kernel OOM-killer.
contributing_factors: Unbounded in-memory queuing during end-of-month batch transaction settlement
JVM MaxRAMPercentage not set, causing Java heap to size based on node rather than cgroup limits
recommended_debugging_steps: kubectl describe pod billing-service-7f89c4d9b-x98pk | grep -A 5 -i oom
Inspect Prometheus container_memory_working_set_bytes metric leading up to 14:10:02Z
Capture JVM heap dump analysis using Eclipse Memory Analyzer (MAT)
suggested_remediation_actions: Implement backpressure or offload batch records to Amazon SQS
Increase Kubernetes memory request/limit to 24Gi with horizontal pod autoscaler (HPA)

baseline_output.root_cause_analysis: Linux OOM-killer terminated the container due to memory cgroup limits exceeded.
contributing_factors: Absence of JVM/Node heap limits inside cgroup
recommended_debugging_steps: Check memory leak in heap profile
